items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...take somebody like Max Roach (PHONETIC) who say, 'Well, hey, I don't see it that way at all.' ... Archie Shepp at Amherst, Max Roach at Amherst

ctx.x: King of Swing, they're serious about that. That is their point of view and they'll take somebody like Max Roach (PHONETIC) who say, "Well, hey, I don't see it that way at all." But his is another point of view. It's a black point of view.

Uh-huh. Well, it's going back to that black-white thing again. You notice most of the critics, they'll say, "Which is the better music? A black one or a white one?" You know, that's just like asking which came first, the chicken or the egg, you know.

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: all of them -- Klook, old man Max, Joe Jones ...

ctx.x: He was playing all those kinds of music?

He'd play everything. The man was a genius. There's no drummer, I think, in the country that came to Chicago and never met Ike or heard of him. I'll tell you, I mean, all of them -- Klook, old man Max, Joe Jones ...
So in addition to being -- to keeping time, as you would say, he was ...
